neighbours.label: the adjective ' special' or the adverb ' particularly' in community, school or charity prose
fire: The garden holds special meaning for the families of our village.
Our Year 5 class particularly loved the trip to the castle.
We are a group of local parents with special interests in music.
The church hall is a place of special importance to older members.
Members who particularly liked last year's fair can volunteer again.
This week the children made cards for someone special in their lives.
The walk is particularly popular with visitors in the spring.
She spoke of her special memories of the old school.
quiet: The garden holds regular meetings for the families of our village.
Our Year 5 class visited the castle on a trip last month.
We are a group of local parents with young children in music.
The church hall is a place of weekly meetings for older members.
Members who attended last year's fair can volunteer again.
This week the children made cards for their friends in other classes.
The walk is open to visitors from the spring onward.
She spoke of her early years at the old school.

notes: Card: ' with' x9, ' special' x7, ' particular' x3, ' particularly', mostly British community and school websites. Probes: special 0.433, particularly 0.400, but ' particular' only 0.085, and the baseline is high: 'have enjoyed' 0.298 and 'with long histories' 0.201. So near misses may fire; the test will show if the words beat the context.
